pr_body:
fix https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/6046

currently stacks on top of https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/6034

---

POC. On top of the magic we do in #6046, this PR's implementation is also drilling into `props.children`. As such, it depends on children inlining, so unlike in #6046, we cannot defer rendering by having the host wrap WelcomeScreen into their own component. Not that we currently do with `<Menu>`, but we could, since we only need to retrieve the top-level `Menu` component.

With WelcomeScreen, we need to separately retrieve `WelcomeScreen.Center`, `WelcomeScreen.MenuHint`, `WelcomeScreen.ToolbarHint`, and `WelcomeScreen.HelpHint` components.

The `<WelcomeScreen>` wrapper isn't even rendered to DOM, it's used just to [retrieve its children](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/6048/files#diff-9a4a11969b4596b06f2a7eb11df1c819d4f17b589d898bed82ff5447ed495978R114-R128) (so effectively it's just a glorified JSX dictionary). As such, we could do away with the wrapper, and have host apps render the `WelcomeScreen` components separately. It comes down to what we think is a better API.

Downside of this approach, as alluded above, is that pretty much the whole `WelcomeScreen` component tree must be rendered in the render function rendering the `<Excalidraw/>` component. This is why I'm [memoizing](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/6048/files#diff-7d537bef2a9bbed4a1fbc825d63163ce532bb20b8ea8dfc0ae1d1b296dcf2aecR647) it for perf (which we should be doing with `<Menu>` in the host app as well btw), because 99% of the time there's no point re-rendering the `WelcomeScreen` tree that's hidden.

- [x] split `WelcomeScreen.tsx` and put into its own folder
- [x] fix mobile breakpoints
- [x] refactor CSS/classes
- [ ] update i18n files (align naming with `en.json` and update Crowdin)
- [x] docs & changelog
- [x] rename welcome-screen folders to kebab-case

Some notes:

- I'm supporting any HTML attributes on the welcomeScreen menu items as there's not reason not to. This way the host app can pass any ARIA or data and other attributes they like. We should do that with `DropdownMenu` as well.
- I didn't add readme examples for every component because there's no need. We should aim for completeness, but also brevity. Excess information is not good either.
- I've made some tiny tweaks to the readme for MainMenu as well, but I bet it will get lost in the migration. I'll do a pass of the docs before we ship them.

issue_context.title: WelcomeScreen API
issue_context.body:
part of https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/5960

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5153846/210066241-6d755d19-e60a-4df2-8ffa-6c74d538b567.png)

### Notes

- If `<WelcomeScreen/>` rendered in host, its children will be the responsibility of host (similar to `<Menu/>`).
- Each `WelcomeScreen.*` arrow child component will have a default content. Host apps can change text by supplying `children`.
- `<WelcomeScreen.Canvas/>`'s `children` will contain more subcomponents, `Logo`, `Tagline`, and `Menu`.

review_comments:
I prefer named exports so that there's a contract in naming —  you can name default imports anything, which isn't good.

But again, we have no styleguide for this
can this not go into `WelcomeScreen` as a `child` since its absolutely positioned?

would be hard to positioning. Also note that relative positioning is great for host apps such as Plus, where we offset the menu button and we get the hint positioning for free. So I'm for keeping as is.
